CS 6672 · hacker presentation

Cornell Time Machine

Twenty years of the campus in one COLMAP model: what changed, when, and which source says so.

Licensed online photographs (Wikimedia Commons, Flickr via Openverse), public New York State aerial flights 2002–2023, USGS lidar 2020, OpenStreetMap footprints, documented dates. No annotation, no geotags, no manual correspondences.

Gates Hall rises from a parking lot · Klarman Hall fills a courtyard · McGraw Tower stays, and anchors the timeline.

The idea

One metric frame, every dated source inside it

  • Frame: public-domain USGS lidar in UTM metres; building footprints from OpenStreetMap.
  • Photographs: COLMAP (pycolmap + SuperPoint + LightGlue) fragments, anchored to the lidar without geotags.
  • Time on every point: each reconstructed point carries the first and last year a photograph observed it (Scene Chronology, rebuilt on pycolmap).
  • Time from above: six aerial flights draped on the lidar terrain; the ground is the 2020 surface, flattened where a building did not yet stand.
  • Documented dates drive the building volumes; the automatic aerial score is shown as a diagnostic, not as the decision.
Live demo: timemachine.html · the slider is the time axis.
Chapter 1 · from above

Six flights, three sites that did not exist in 2002

Each flight is warped onto the lidar grid; the crops below are the same footprint in every year.

Gates Hall site — parking lot, then a building from the 2015 flight.

Klarman Hall site — the courtyard behind Goldwin Smith Hall, excavation in 2015, a roof from 2018.

New York State orthoimagery, NYS GIS Program Office (public).
Chapter 2 · Gates Hall

A parking lot until 2012, a building from 2014

  • Documented: construction began March 2012, occupied early 2014, dedicated October 2014.
  • From the air: absent in the 2012 flight, present from 2015; the own-outline edge score rises from 2.4 to 4.0–5.7.
  • From the ground: its photographs are being reconstructed and anchored through the building's footprint.
  • In the demo the slider flattens the site before 2012, shows the works, then the lidar volume, and the photographers of each year.
Chapter 3 · Klarman Hall

The courtyard fills, and a limit shows itself

  • Documented: completed 2016, built between the back of Goldwin Smith Hall and East Avenue.
  • From the air: courtyard through 2012, excavation in 2015, roof from 2018 (score 2.0–2.4, then 3.7–4.1).
  • From the ground: the fifteen licensed photographs around Goldwin Smith Hall see its portico and the A. D. White statue from the lawn. Without the tower in view, one facade cannot fix its own scale: the portico shrunk onto a nine-metre wing wall fits the walls as well as the portico at its own fifteen-metre wall. Reported as not anchored.
A negative with a reason is a result: the chapter rests on the flights and the documented dates, and says so.
Chapter 4 · McGraw Tower

The thing that does not change, measured

  • 63 photographs of the tower and Uris Library in one model, 25 with capture dates from 2003 to 2025.
  • Anchored to the lidar through the tower: gravity from facade normals, the tower as the tallest cluster on its footprint, scale from photographers at eye height against the measured tower top, one yaw from the walls. Two independent scales agree within 2 %.
  • Every point carries the years it was seen; the slider replays them, "colour by first year" shows when each surface entered the record.
  • Click a photographer to see the photograph and its licence.
Under the hood · COLMAP extended

Four things stock COLMAP does not do

ExtensionWhat it addsChecked by
EXIF-anchored calibrationcameras with an EXIF focal length held constant; the rest refined in a tight windowfocal outliers gone; fragments did not merge, so content, not calibration, split the scene
Landmark anchoringa fragment placed in UTM metres through the tower's footprint, lidar top and standing photographersa second, horizontal scale from the library walls: 2 % apart
Footprint anchoringfragments without the tower placed through one building's walls (precision and recall of wall coverage) and lidar roof edgesa synthetic hall with a known similarity: scale within 3 %, yaw within 0.1°, photographers within 2 m; the walls-only scale, the other yaw quadrants and photographer heights reported
Existence intervalsfirst and last observing year per point; per-building first-photographed yeardated photographs only; undated ones observe but do not date

All on CPU: pycolmap 3.13, hloc with SuperPoint and LightGlue, NetVLAD retrieval, batched matching inside 7.6 GB of RAM.

Honesty

Measured, documented, or diagnostic: the page says which

  • Measured: lidar heights, anchored points and photographer positions, existence intervals, the aerial images themselves.
  • Documented: the construction dates (cited), which decide when a volume appears.
  • Diagnostic: the own-outline aerial score. It rises at every site when the building appears, but stable buildings vary between flights by as much, so it is shown next to the crops and never decides.
  • Reported, not hidden: the anchor's failed checks, the fragment that would not anchor, the mirror-image Boardman poses from the earlier work.
Limits and next

What the record cannot show

  • No licensed ground-level photograph of any site before construction exists online: the "before" is aerial only.
  • A single facade cannot fix its scale without a landmark, a second facade, or a photographer standing somewhere known.
  • Commons throttles originals to roughly one every ten minutes; the collections are still growing.
  • Next: dense textured surfaces per site from post-construction photographs; tower-top photographs placed on the belfry; the negative evidence of absence (a registered camera that should have seen a building and did not).
Reproducible

Public data in, every number traceable out

  • Stages under pipeline/ghostmap/: acquire → prepare → sfm → anchor → chronology → web → qa; each writes a JSON report the page reads.
  • Inputs: Commons and Openverse (licence recorded per photo), NYS orthoimagery WMS, USGS 3DEP lidar, OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Wikipedia for the dates.
  • Checks in the repository: 344 unit tests, Playwright checks of every chapter and year.
